changes.currentBefore: A visible central scar is typically T2 bright and enhances extracellular contrast on delay. This differs from hepatobiliary uptake of the remaining FNH tissue; a scar is not obligatory.
changes.after: A visible central scar is typically T2 bright and shows delayed enhancement with extracellular contrast. This differs from hepatobiliary uptake of the remaining FNH tissue; a scar is not obligatory.

changes.currentBefore: Im Gegensatz zum Hämangiom zeigt die FNH eine rasche, homogene arterielle Anreicherung, ohne periphere noduläre Aufnahme oder zentripetale Auffüllung.
changes.after: Im Vergleich zum klassischen Hämangiommuster zeigt typische FNH eine rasche, homogene arterielle Anreicherung statt diskontinuierlicher peripherer Kontrastknoten mit späterer zentripetaler Auffüllung.

changes.currentBefore: Unlike haemangioma, FNH shows rapid, homogeneous arterial enhancement without peripheral nodular enhancement or centripetal fill-in.
changes.after: Compared with the classic haemangioma pattern, typical FNH shows rapid, homogeneous arterial enhancement rather than discontinuous peripheral nodules with later centripetal fill-in.

changes.currentBefore: A visible central scar is usually T2 hyperintense and T1 hypointense and enhances extracellular contrast on delay. It may be absent or not visible, particularly in small FNH.
changes.after: A visible central scar is usually T2 hyperintense and T1 hypointense and shows delayed enhancement with extracellular contrast. It may be absent or not visible, particularly in small FNH.
